memories.content: Use a flow diagram rather than a sequence table when alternate procedural branches lead to different outcomes.
Draw alternate branches and their resulting outcomes in the same flow diagram so readers can compare them at once.
The visual fidelity of a prototype may differ from its functional fidelity.
A flow diagram can make alternate branches and their different outcomes visible in one view.
HCI reviewers often skim prototype screens and interaction flow diagrams before reading the main text.
Readers can understand the overall branching shape of a procedure more quickly from a flow diagram than from rows read one at a time.
Redrawing a branching flow diagram after a procedural change usually takes longer than updating one row in a table.
Reviewers often inspect the proposal’s main visual before reading the procedural explanation in full.
Specify a single representative measure that will drive operational decisions to maintain, modify, or discontinue the deployed design.
The HCI review panel verifies whether operational decisions can be made based on the declared primary measure.
Establish decision thresholds indicating at what levels key metrics trigger maintaining, modifying, or discontinuing the design.
Evaluate whether reducing workload for one role creates new tasks for other roles through the proposed design changes.
Distinguish usability from organizational adoption intent as separate evaluation outcomes.
Implementation fidelity indicates whether planned features and operational procedures were delivered in the field according to intended specifications.
Initial evaluations and long-term operation do not share identical measurement conditions due to differences in system exposure duration and frequency of repeated use.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate concerns without contradiction: the reference focuses on communicating branching procedures, prototype fidelity, review behavior, and diagram maintenance, while the compared frame focuses on field-evaluation measures, decision rules, workload redistribution, adoption, implementation fidelity, and changing measurement conditions.

relations.reason: These statements collectively express the reference-only rationale and presentation policy for using flow diagrams when procedural branches produce different outcomes.
relations.summary: Branching procedures are best communicated in a single flow diagram that exposes alternate paths and outcomes together and supports faster structural understanding than row-by-row reading.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only distinction between two dimensions of prototype fidelity.
relations.summary: A prototype’s visual fidelity and functional fidelity may differ.

relations.reason: These statements restate a reference-only observation about reviewers prioritizing key visuals during initial inspection.
relations.summary: Reviewers often inspect prominent prototype or proposal visuals and interaction-flow materials before reading the full explanatory text.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only maintenance tradeoff associated with flow diagrams.
relations.summary: Updating a branching flow diagram after a procedural change generally takes longer than changing a single table row.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only policy for selecting the primary operational decision measure.
relations.summary: A single representative measure should drive decisions to maintain, modify, or discontinue a deployed design.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only review responsibility concerning the decision usefulness of the primary measure.
relations.summary: The HCI review panel checks whether the declared primary measure can support operational decisions.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only requirement for explicit operational decision thresholds.
relations.summary: Key metrics should have thresholds that trigger maintaining, modifying, or discontinuing the design.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only evaluation criterion concerning redistribution of work across roles.
relations.summary: Evaluation should determine whether workload reductions for one role create new tasks for other roles.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only distinction between evaluation outcomes.
relations.summary: Usability and organizational adoption intent should be evaluated as separate outcomes.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only definition of field implementation fidelity, distinct from prototype visual and functional fidelity.
relations.summary: Implementation fidelity concerns whether planned features and operational procedures were delivered in the field as intended.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only qualification about how evaluation conditions change over time.
relations.summary: Initial evaluation and long-term operation have different measurement conditions because exposure duration and repeated-use frequency differ.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame defines operational evaluation governance, including primary measures, thresholds, reviewability, cross-role workload effects, separate adoption outcomes, implementation fidelity, and evaluation conditions that change over time.
reports.reference_only: The reference emphasizes flow diagrams for rapidly comparing procedural branches and outcomes, while noting reviewer attention patterns, distinct prototype fidelity dimensions, and diagram-update costs.
